name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DispatchInputToChildren
summary: UI input handler: for confirm/cancel events it marks the widget dirty and requests state 0 from the controller at +0x120 (slot +0x14, then commit +0x10); for plain movement events it forwards the three signed axes to the navigation object at +0x980 slot +0x3C. Always returns 1.
evidence: Unchanged: the body is intact and the event masking (0x142 / 4 / 1) plus the three-axis forwarding are verified, but the controller at +0x120 and the navigation object at +0x980 are still unnamed and the function has no callers, so neither the 'Ui_Widget' owner nor the 'to children' wording can be confirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DispatchInputByState
summary: Variant input handler for a widget with a 3-state controller: 0x00642630(self+0x260, event) returns 0/1/2 and selects the child action 1/2/3 before the same mark-dirty/notify tail; movement events go to the +0x260 slot +0x3C.
evidence: Unchanged: the callee 0x00642630 resolves into maybe_Ui_Window_SetStateMessageArgs (0x00642508), i.e. an inner entry of a misnamed window helper, so it does not explain the 0/1/2 state values. The name still describes only the shape of the body.

name: Ui_EquipRow_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the equipment row widget: installs the base vtable 0x00758AE0 (the shared 0x00193E44 block) and frees the object through the allocator at 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: CORRECTED: the class is not a generic 'Ui_Panel'. 0x002EA468 is slot 0 of the vtable 0x007614C8, whose +0x3C row is the confident Ui_EquipRow_Update (0x002EB3B4) and whose +0x30 row is 0x002EB618 - so this is the equipment row class, the same family as maybe_Ui_EquipRow_RangeCheck (0x002EBB08). The eight callers are deleting destructors of widgets that own an equip row (Ui_TalkSubWidget, Field_ActorMotion, maybe_Battle_DamagePopup, ...), which is why the old name guessed a shared panel base.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ApplyValueToChildren
summary: Walks both child containers of a UI window (self+0x10 and self+0x14: four fixed slots each plus their variable child list) and writes the same value into every child's +0x70 field.
evidence: Unchanged: the entry is 2-mod-4 (a mid-function Thumb block) and its only caller is Ui_Dive_ReloadTextResources (0x002EA9F2), so the loop shape is visible but the meaning of the +0x70 field and the 'Ui_Window' owner are not established.

name: maybe_Container_AddToFirstFreeSlot
signature: void* maybe_Container_AddToFirstFreeSlot(Container* c, u8 kind, u32 forwarded, u32 second)
summary: Finds the first free slot among five fixed 9-word slots (empty = the global null handle at 0x007A8A44), stores the kind byte at +0x18, configures the slot through its vtable +0xC and links it into the container list at +0xC0.
evidence: Unchanged: the body is intact and the five-way slot search, the 9-word stride and the list splice are all verified, but the splice helper 0x001235A4 resolves into the misnamed Snd_DetachChannel and the only caller is maybe_Map_AddInstanceIfVisible, so the container's owner stays generic.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipRow_RangeCheck
summary: Compares the row's cursor with the end marker of its item list; the decompiler lost the real body after the comparison.
evidence: Unchanged: the body is halt_baddata plus a bogus func_0xff7e4072 call, so only `if (*f_C4 != f_C0)` is certain. The Ui_EquipRow family is now confirmed by the named Ui_EquipRow_Update (0x002EB3B4) and Ui_EquipRow_DeletingDtor (0x002EA468), which supports the prefix, but the operation itself is still unreadable.

name: maybe_Container_UnlinkAndReleaseHandles
summary: Empties a handle list: for each registered entry it resolves the handle's type through the global table at 0x007B5D70, tests liveness, unlinks the node and rewrites the handle word to drop the reference.
evidence: Unchanged: the recovered C is a single garbage expression (in_r12 + unaff_r4*0x1000000) and the four callees resolve into unrelated named functions (Gfx_CommandBuffer_Submit, Ui_Widget_CountChildren, Ui_Casino_InitRouletteWheel, Ui_ListText_GetFirstKnownItemId), i.e. they are inner entries of shared blocks. Everything above still comes from the earlier disassembly notes.

name: Anim_ClipSlot_InitLinearMotion
summary: Initialises the non-arcing clip-slot variant: runs the shared slot init 0x0028B3AC, stores the amount at +0x3C and starts the clip named "Nut" on the sprite pane at +0x28.
evidence: NEW: the variant is confirmed by the vtable 0x007615E0 this function is slot 0 of - its +0x08 row is the confident Anim_ClipSlot_UpdateLinearMotion (0x002EBE78), so the 'LinearMotion' label no longer depends on the clip string. The class is the same one whose base sub-object vtable 0x00761610 holds maybe_Anim_ClipSlot_DeletingDtorBase.

name: Anim_ClipSlot_DeletingDtorLinear
summary: Deleting destructor of the non-arcing clip-slot variant: installs the base vtable 0x00758AE0 (shared 0x00193E40 block) and frees the object.
evidence: NEW: 0x002EBEEC is slot 0 of the vtable 0x007615DC, whose +0x04 row is Anim_ClipSlot_InitLinearMotion and whose +0x0C row is the confident Anim_ClipSlot_UpdateLinearMotion (0x002EBE78) - so this really is the deleting destructor of the LinearMotion variant, not just a guess from the neighbouring Init/Update pair.

name: Anim_ClipSlot_DeletingDtorBase
summary: Deleting destructor of the base clip-slot sub-object (the one with no motion driver of its own): installs the base vtable 0x00758AE0 and frees the object.
evidence: NEW: 0x002EBF3C is slot 0 of the vtable 0x00761610, which is the table of the sub-object embedded at +0x30 of the LinearMotion clip-slot class (0x007615E0); its other rows are the plain slot methods 0x0028B3AC/0x0028B6AC/0x0028B3D4, i.e. no motion driver - which is exactly the 'base' reading. The confident Anim_ClipSlot_UpdateLinearMotion sibling fixes the family.
